hints: Focus on what the physical state tells you, as Period 3 oxides change from solids to gases across the period.
Sulfur dioxide does form an acidic solution, but think carefully about whether it is a solid or a gas at 25 degrees.
Compare the two white solids that are acidic, and remember which one actually dissolves and reacts with water.
walkthrough:
**Sort by state at 25 degrees**

Think across Period 3 from left to right. The oxides go from giant solids to simple molecular solids and gases.

$\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ is a white solid, $\text{SiO}_2$ is a white solid, $\text{P}_4\text{O}_{10}$ is a white solid, but $\text{SO}_2$ is a colourless gas at $25^\circ\text{C}$. So sulfur dioxide cannot be X.

**Sort by acid-base behaviour with water**

Remember the trend: basic to amphoteric to acidic across the period. Aluminium oxide is amphoteric but insoluble, so it does not give an acidic solution. Silicon dioxide is weakly acidic but it is insoluble and does not react with water.

Only the non-metal oxides higher up react to give acids:
$$\text{P}_4\text{O}_{10} + 6\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow 4\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4$$

**Match both clues together**

We need a white solid that reacts with water to make an acid. Phosphorus(V) oxide fits both perfectly. It is a white flaky solid and it reacts vigorously to form phosphoric acid, a strongly acidic solution.

options.A: Aluminium oxide is a white solid, but it is amphoteric and essentially insoluble in water. It does not dissolve to form an acidic solution, so it fails the second clue.
options.B: Silicon dioxide is a white solid with acidic character, but it has a giant covalent structure. It is insoluble and does not react with water, so no acidic solution is formed.
options.C: Sulfur dioxide does react with water to form sulfurous acid, which is acidic. However it is a gas at 25 degrees, not a white solid, so it fails the first clue.
options.D: Phosphorus(V) oxide, $\text{P}_4\text{O}_{10}$, is a white solid at 25 degrees and reacts vigorously with water to give phosphoric acid, $\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4$. This matches both the state and the acidic solution perfectly.
